items.title: Hausdorff dimension n-2 of the symmetric boundary of a strictly convex projective domain with C1 boundary
items.author: Olivier Glorieux; Daniel Monclair; Nicolas Tholozan
items.work: Hausdorff dimension of limit sets for projective Anosov representations
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.241
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the Hausdorff dimension of the symmetric boundary partial Omega^sym = {(x,x*) : x in partial Omega} of a strictly convex projective domain with C^1 boundary, where the duality homeomorphism x -> x* is not C^1 unless the boundary is C^2, so the dimension of its graph is not immediate (the authors say so at source line 1014). The proof chooses two boundary points, identifies an affine patch with V x R, writes the boundary as the graph of a C^1 strictly convex function f, computes the dual point (u,f(u))* = (-d_uf, d_uf(u) - f(u)) and reduces the claim to the set {(u, d_uf)} in V x V*. The step that cannot be done routinely is the dimension bound itself: the authors introduce the symmetric bilinear form <(u,alpha),(v,beta)> = alpha(v) + beta(u) of signature (n-2,n-2), prove that difference vectors of the set have strictly positive square using d_uf(v-u) < f(v) - f(u), and then combine injectivity of the orthogonal projection onto a spacelike subspace with Brouwer's invariance of domain to exhibit the set as a 1-Lipschitz graph of dimension n-2 (source lines 1043-1060).
